provenance.v6_change: fresh development/validation takes; ball-identity appearance consistency added before any fresh validation is opened

diagnosis: component circularity used connected-component pixel area with contour perimeter and produced impossible values >1
candidate ranking favored longer full-flight intervals, allowing slow same-object reset motion to outrank the fast gravity event

provenance.v6_1_change: development-only correction before fresh validation: bounded contour geometry/solidity/circle-fill/axis-ratio/radius stability; rank fastest ball-like release-from-rest full-travel event instead of longest; gates/repair schedule/|S| unchanged

diagnosis: bounded geometry was fixed, but identity_score remained the first lexicographic ranking term
high-identity slow same-ball traversals still won on takes with 71-frame and 31-frame selected intervals
identity should be an eligibility gate; event ranking must operate on near-full-span candidates and prioritize fastest full travel

provenance.v6_2_change: development-only selector correction: require candidate span >=70% of the maximum eligible ball span in the video, then rank by shortest full-flight duration before timing/shape residuals; emit top-candidate audit; gates/repair schedule/|S| unchanged

v6_2_implementation_error.root_cause: fit_full_flight_progress returned None for short tracks while choose_ballistic_track unconditionally extended the result
v6_2_implementation_error.experimental_interpretation: none; no take produced a selected candidate and this run is classified as software failure, not scientific evidence
v6_2_implementation_error.fix: candidate producer now has total list return contract; selector validates producer return type/candidate schema/finite fields; unexpected exceptions are saved with traceback and force gate false

diagnosis: 70% relative-span rule selected slow reset/handling because reset covered the largest image-space extent
fast gravity candidates on 06,07,09,10 were rejected for smaller local span even though they had much shorter durations
partial gravity fragments must be timed in a global full-drop coordinate rather than interpreted as 100% of the physical drop

provenance.v6_3_change: development-only redesign: estimate full top-bottom pixel envelope from all ball-like motion, use reset only as spatial calibration, keep only downward gravity-direction fragments, fit t=t0+T*sqrt(p_global) in global progress coordinates, and rank by global timing/shape fit; target g remains absent from selection

v6_3_implementation_error.root_cause: V6.3 fragment rejection branches called a helper that existed only in a different legacy function scope; legacy recalibration also referenced diagnostics without declaring it
v6_3_implementation_error.experimental_interpretation: none; all five takes crashed before scientific evaluation
v6_3_implementation_error.fix: module-level _reject helper; explicit diagnostics signatures; rejection-path self-tests; pyflakes in CI and local preflight

v6_3_second_implementation_error.error: RuntimeError: selected full-flight window violates minimum duration
v6_3_second_implementation_error.experimental_interpretation: none for the affected takes; the downstream duration check was incompatible with V6.3 partial-fragment semantics
diagnosis: V6.3 selector enforced inferred full duration T*fps >= minimum_active_frames
extract() incorrectly re-applied the old rule to observed fragment sample count
the quality gate duplicated the same obsolete assumption via active_frames

provenance.v6_4_change: development-only redesign before validation: separate observed fragment frames from inferred full-fall duration; identify release and impact stationary plateaus around downward ball motion; infer T from release->impact timing; validate normalized p(t)~(t/T)^2; ignore later upward reset timing; gates/repair schedule/|S| unchanged

diagnosis: release/impact plateau matching rejected takes 06, 07, and 09 despite valid ball-like motion candidates
accepted takes 08 and 10 inferred 15-16 frame full falls and produced 43-63% acceleration error
the remaining estimator still used 2h/T^2, which assumes the observed interval is anchored to zero-velocity release; development evidence shows the tracker often observes an interior flight fragment

provenance.v6_5_change: development-only redesign before fresh validation: retain ball identity and global top-bottom spatial calibration; fit p(t)=a+b t+0.5 c t^2 on the observed gravity-direction motion with nuisance position/velocity; exclude stationary holds from the kinematic fit; require sufficient observed moving-frame support rather than exact release/impact observation; treat full-event roots and release-rest timing as optional diagnostics; rank without target gravity; use c*drop_height as the primary development acceleration diagnostic; development/validation gates, repair schedule, and |S|=2 remain unchanged

diagnosis: all five clips passed appearance/trajectory quality while the primary acceleration estimate remained 72-100% wrong, falsifying V6.5 image-space metric calibration
the largest same-ball image excursion was used as the 0.5 m ruler even though it can be manual reset/handling motion rather than release-to-impact travel
V6.5 disabled the release-speed quality gate and admitted selected candidates with release-speed ratios up to 11.266
candidate ranking prioritized global image-progress span ahead of acceleration stability, allowing slow/manual trajectories to win

provenance.v6_6_change: development-only redesign before fresh validation: remove manual-reset image span from the primary gravity estimate; identify a positive constant-pixel-acceleration ballistic run, infer release from its velocity-zero vertex, infer impact from the terminal speed collapse/reversal or track end, and compute g solely from independently measured drop height and release-to-impact time g=2h/T^2. Target gravity remains absent from candidate generation/ranking; validation/final data remain unopened.

diagnosis: metric-free event timing substantially improved the V6.5 median error but still failed the frozen 20% development gate
take 09 recovered a 19.739-frame fall and 5.78% gravity error, showing the 2h/T^2 timing estimator is sound when release/impact boundaries are correct
takes 06, 08, and 10 terminated at 14-16 frames and produced spuriously high gravity, indicating track-local plateaus were mistaken for physical impact after temporal fragmentation
the next revision must bind stationary release/impact evidence across track IDs rather than retune the gravity threshold or target magnitude

provenance.v6_7_change: development-only boundary-stitching revision: keep V6.6 metric-free g=2h/T^2, but allow ball-identity-qualified stationary release/impact plateaus from different temporal track IDs to bracket a partial falling fragment. Candidate selection uses temporal order, spatial continuity, release-from-rest trajectory shape, timing residual, and identity only; target gravity remains absent. Fresh drop_100 validation and final data remain unopened.
